variant_perception_summary: The market has re-rated DHER >130% on Uber's acquisition approach and is pricing an ~11.6% arbitrage spread to an offer price that is NOT confirmed anywhere in the primary data pool. Layered underneath that unverified spread sits a hard auditor going-concern disqualifier, GAAP-basis leverage already past an illustrative 6x refinancing ceiling, 'Poor'-quality cash-light earnings (Critical concerns), and a serial-acquirer capital-allocation record -- a risk cluster that deal euphoria appears to be discounting less than the primary evidence supports.
what_everyone_knows: Uber announced an acquisition approach for Delivery Hero on 2026-07-16; Prosus/Naspers has irrevocably committed to tender its stake; the deal is guided to close in H2 2027; DHER stock has risen from EUR15.73 (pre-announcement) to EUR37.20.
what_is_priced_in: A high probability of deal completion near a widely-reported (but not primary-sourced) ~EUR41.50/share cash price, reflected in an ~11.6% arbitrage spread and a Target Price consensus (EUR37.97 mean) that the earnings module itself flags as deal-contaminated.
what_market_may_be_missing: (1) The offer price itself is unverified in every primary source reviewed -- no M&A call transcript, filing, or exchange notice in this pool states a fixed per-share consideration; (2) the auditor's own going-concern note on Glovo Spain, the GAAP-basis leverage already past the balance-sheet module's own stress-test ceiling, and management's personal change-of-control vesting conflict are all live, unresolved risks that a clean arbitrage read tends to discount away once a deal is announced.
edge_proof: Falsifiable test: if Uber's tender completes within the guided H2 2027 window at a confirmed cash price at or above EUR41.50/share, with no minority squeeze-out dispute and the FY2025 audited Annual Report (once published) shows the Glovo Spain going-concern language resolved or removed, this thesis's risk read is wrong and the engine underweighted a well-flagged, well-committed strategic transaction. If the deal stalls, breaks, or completes materially below EUR41.50, or the going-concern language persists/escalates, the thesis is confirmed.
killer_risk: A blocked or broken Uber deal (no confirmed price, no disclosed break fee in the pool) sending the stock back toward standalone risk, while the auditor-flagged Glovo Spain going-concern liability (up to EUR770m) and GAAP-basis net leverage (8.24x, already above the balance-sheet module's own illustrative 6.0x refinancing ceiling) remain unresolved.

red_flags.description: Auditor going-concern note (KPMG) -- subsidiary-level 'Material Uncertainty about the Ability of Subsidiaries to Continue as a Going Concern,' Glovo Spain rider-classification risk, contingent liability EUR440-770m; hard disqualifier locks the business-model verdict at 'Low-quality business -- avoid deeper work.'
Governance risk floored at 80/100 via Disqualifier Deference on the same going-concern note; stewardship verdict capped at 'Serious governance concerns.'

FY2025 cash-conversion collapse (CFO/Adjusted EBITDA 8.8%) and the '+EUR250m FCF' headline exclude an implied ~EUR600-650m cash outflow tied to the same going-concern-adjacent Glovo Spain exposure -- the connection was made only by 08_earnings-red-flags, not by earnings agents 00-07.
The identical FCF-exclusion methodology stands as FY2026 guidance policy; a recurring outflow could let the FY2026 print look 'on guide' while cash generation disappoints.

Serial-acquirer pattern -- EUR2,054m cumulative goodwill impairment FY2021-2025 against the Woowa (~$4.0bn) and Glovo (EUR2.3bn) mega-deals; caps capital allocation at 50 and floors governance risk at 60 (superseded by the higher disqualifier floor of 80).

Turnaround claimed without >=2-3 years delivered operating inflection on the statutory metric -- only 1 clean fiscal year (FY2025) of positive GAAP operating profit after 4 years of losses; management quality capped at 60.

Change-of-control provision fully and unconditionally vests all Management Board members' unvested equity on resignation within 3 months of a change of control -- a personal, price-independent incentive to see the pending Uber deal close.
The absolute FY2025 statutory net loss (-EUR782.9m) was never spoken aloud on the earnings call; only the EUR183m YoY improvement was verbalized.
Goodwill impairment recorded in every one of the last 5 fiscal years; GAAP-to-Adjusted-EBITDA gap is 66% of the adjusted figure in FY2025 and exceeds 100% in FY2024.
Cash conversion (CFO/Adjusted EBITDA) at 8.8% FY2025; 2 of the last 3 fiscal years below 50%.
Spain rider-reclassification contingent liability: EUR520-860m unrecognized (FY2025) on top of EUR492.2m already provisioned (FY2024) and EUR524.0m already paid (FY2025) for the same matter.

Fast-changing industry / disruption risk (rate-of-change score 26/100, <=40 threshold, CLAUDE.md Section 24 Filter 5) -- thesis flagged as a sector/technology-cycle bet; the industry is still being sorted by live M&A (DoorDash-Deliveroo, Uber-DHER itself).

Cross-module forensic mosaic per CLAUDE.md Section 13: RF-EQ-002 (earnings) + RF-OBS-001 (balance-sheet-survival) + RF-DISC-001 + RF-DISC-002 (management-governance) = 4 distinct tags across 3 modules. Compounds into a single High accounting-integrity flag. Does not further restrict the headline since 'Avoid' is already more conservative than the 'Starter Position Only' ceiling this cap would otherwise impose on a Buy-side rating.

notes: This is fundamentally a merger-arbitrage situation layered on top of a hard-disqualified standalone business. The current price is deal-contaminated (up >130% since the pre-announcement close of EUR15.73); every valuation/margin-of-safety read in this file is as much a bet on Uber's undisclosed deal terms as on DHER's own fundamentals. Expected return, downside risk, and risk/reward are all computed off a scenario set that blends deal-completion odds (self-constructed by the master synthesizer, since no module assigns deal probabilities) with the valuation module's own standalone bull/base/bear levels. The single most fragile assumption in this file is the ~EUR41.50/share reported offer price -- it is UNVERIFIED and not in the data pool; every base-case/bull-case number here inherits that fragility.
